Treasury Secretary Bessent forecasts fiscal consolidation:

Bessent said fiscal contraction would have continued but for tariff refunds and confirmed that additional fiscal consolidation is forthcoming. He also addressed AI regulation, stating that creators of advanced AI models should bear legal responsibility for safety rather than receiving "a blank check on liability."
Empire State manufacturing growth cools in September:
The New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Index

to 7.6 in September from 20.6 in August, missing the 14.1 consensus. While the headline figure remained in positive territory, new orders slowed sharply to 2.0 from 17.3 and shipments turned negative at -3.2. Pricing pressures intensified, with prices paid rising to 63.1 from 58.6 and prices received climbing to 28.1 from 22.7. Employment grew at a solid pace, with the number of employees index edging up to 10.6 from 9.3.
RTX projects durable growth on defense backlog and air travel:

Chairman and CEO Chris Calio  told Morgan Stanley's annual Laguna Conference that the aerospace and defense company holds a backlog of approximately $289 billion, excluding five major munitions framework agreements and a recently awarded seven-year, $23 billion Tomahawk contract. Calio projected medium-term operating margins of 19%-20% for Collins Aerospace and 2026 free cash flow of about $8.6 billion. About 48% of Raytheon's backlog is international, up four percentage points from a year earlier, as geopolitical tensions drive increased defense spending globally.
FDA launches pilot to accelerate drug clinical trial approvals:

The U.S. FDA  announced the Expedited IND Pilot Program under HHS' Operation TrialBlazer, designed to shorten the time from drug identification to first-in-human trials. The initiative allows rolling component reviews with qualified research institutions rather than waiting for all application components before review begins. The FDA noted that U.S. first-in-human trials currently take up to two years, considerably slower than in China and Australia. Applications are being accepted through Oct. 30, with the agency expecting to select eight to 10 sponsor-institution pairs.
